correctness.rationale: Finite poset equality blocks are convex and Hasse-connected; their fitted values are weighted means. The polyhedral least-squares projection is continuous and piecewise linear, giving a maximum over induced weighted rank-one maps. Conversely, every convex-connected block has an acyclic quotient, and positive active multipliers give a locally stable face realizing its full operator norm. Weighted Hölder yields the exact formula, endpoint conventions, and componentwise proportionality equality classification. Independent exact-rational checks reproduce 84 graph/mass cases, 1164 candidate blocks, 1152 feasible partitions and 63 rigidity cases; enumeration is not a proof for arbitrary finite orders.

value.rationale: Exact stability under distinct fitting and reporting weights is motivated by heteroscedastic order-constrained estimation and post-fit error assessment. The theorem turns a nonlinear global data-to-fit sensitivity into attained weighted pool norms on every finite partial order and gives a complete nonexpansivity rigidity classification, with sharp two-point obstructions. It is not merely one observed numerical example or a rephrasing of an old contraction statement.
